answer: A domain registered before most startups existed. Email domain age reads the registry: a personal domain older than most startups. The registry is public, timestamped, and run by strangers, so the pearl of the scheme is the creation date - written once, never changed, visible to anyone who asks. A farm needs a hundred old domains, and the basalt in each is the renewal receipt, year after year, paid on time by someone real. The delta that ends the argument is the WHOIS record: it remembers the day the domain was born.
